candidates.region: RUNX2 Runt and PST domains (folded domains, not a short linear motif)
concerns: folded-domain interface: large buried surface, poor small-molecule tractability compared with a short linear motif

claims.statement: MED23 physically associates with RUNX2 by co-immunoprecipitation in transfected 293T cells and by endogenous co-immunoprecipitation in differentiated MC3T3E1 osteoblastic cells. The two proteins largely colocalize in the nucleus.
claims.note: PMC4821994 L23. Endogenous co-IP, not only a co-transfection artifact.

claims.statement: The interaction with MED23 is mediated via the Runt and PST domains of RUNX2. A GST pull-down assay using GST-RUNX2 from E. coli against His-Flag-MED23 purified from baculovirus implied the interaction is likely direct.
claims.note: PMC4821994 L23, verified against source text 2026-08-15. This is the mapped interacting region required by the contact rule in CLAUDE.md. The source hedges: it says the pull-down 'implied' the interaction was 'likely' direct. Recorded at the source's own confidence, not upgraded.

claims.statement: Med23 deletion in mesenchymal stem cells or osteoblast precursors produces bone defects resembling Runx2 heterozygous mice; Med23 deficiency reduces Runx2-target-gene activity without changing Runx2 expression; combined Runx2 +/- and Med23 MSC-/- mice show aggravated defects.
claims.note: PMC4821994 L6, L25. Establishes the MED23-RUNX2 axis in NORMAL osteogenic development. This is a safety liability, not a cancer dependency — RUNX2 haploinsufficiency causes cleidocranial dysplasia.

candidates.region: ELK1 transactivation domain, MED23-binding motif (MBM) residues 374-384, sequence PSIHFWSTLS(p)P

claims.statement: Cryo-EM structure at 3.0 A of human MED23 bound to the phosphorylated ELK1 transactivation domain. The ELK1 MED23-binding motif (residues 374-384) binds the concave face of the MED23 core at the HR2/HR3 interface, in a site formed by helices H19, H21, H28 and H30.
claims.note: PDB 9F6Y, EMD-50242. Apo MED23 is PDB 9F76 / EMD-50247.

claims.statement: ELK1 I376, F378 and L382 form the hydrophobic contacts with MED23. F378 binds deeply and is buried, sheltered by adjacent H377 and W379, and is surrounded in MED23 by I339 and L343 (H19), F379, G382 and S383 (H21), and V533 and M537 (H28).
claims.note: These MED23 residues define the pocket a small molecule would have to occupy. Helix assignment corrected 2026-08-15: V533 and M537 are in H28, not H30, verified against PMC12015215 L23.

claims.statement: ELK1 phosphorylated at S383 binds MED23 with a Kd of 81 nM by SPR, while only minimal interaction is detected by pull-down without phosphorylation. Mutation of the central FW motif abolishes the interaction.
claims.note: Binding is phosphorylation-dependent; any screen against this site inherits that condition.

claims.statement: The designed MED23 G382F mutation disrupts ELK1 binding and impairs ELK1-dependent serum-induced activation of target genes in MED23-null MEFs.
claims.note: Point mutation in the pocket produces the expected loss of function, so occupancy of this site is coupled to transcriptional output.

candidates.region: POU2F3 LEELE motif, residues 188-192, in the alpha-1 helix of the POU-specific (POU_S) domain; secondary contact at conserved leucines L235 and L237 in the alpha3-alpha4 turn

claims.statement: Structures of POU2F3 DNA-binding domain bound to the coactivator OCA-T1 (POU2AF2) and to OCA-T2 (POU2AF3) on DNA reveal a tripartite POU2F3-OCA-DNA interface. The POU2F3 LEELE motif at residues 188-192 in the alpha-1 helix of the POU_S domain contacts the OCA peptide, with additional contacts from conserved leucines L235 and L237 in the turn connecting the alpha3 and alpha4 helices.
claims.note: PDB 9PFP (OCA-T1 complex), 9PFN and 9PFO (OCA-T2 complex, low and high resolution). Retrieved via Paperclip 2026-08-15.

claims.statement: Alanine substitutions in the POU2F3 LEELE motif - L188A, E189A, L191A and E192A - impair binding to OCA-T1. An interaction-deficient OCA-T1 V22E mutant is used as a negative control.
claims.note: Point mutations in the mapped motif produce loss of binding, so occupancy of this surface is coupled to the interaction.

claims.statement: The structure reveals a shallow but highly conserved groove on POU2F3 that cradles the OCA peptide, described by the authors as a potential ligandable surface. CASTpFold analysis identifies a surface-exposed pocket of approximately 1022 cubic Angstroms and a smaller 38 cubic Angstrom pocket within the DNA major groove bordered by the ordered OCA-T1 coil.
claims.note: Pocket volumes are a CASTpFold computation on the experimental structure, not a measured binding site. Ligandability is a prediction and must not be reported as demonstrated druggability.

claims.statement: Approximately 15% of small cell lung cancers express POU2F3 and other tuft cell markers, termed SCLC-P. POU2F3 is essential for the growth of these cells in vitro but dispensable in other SCLC subtypes. POU2F3-positive tuft cell-like cancers also occur in thymus, prostate, bladder, colon, pancreas and pharynx.
claims.note: This is the subpopulation-dependency pattern that team/FINDINGS_DEPMAP_ROUND01.md section 4 shows our median-based gate structurally cannot detect: essential in one molecular subtype, dispensable in the rest of the same lineage.

candidates.region: FOXO4 conserved region 3 (CR3), the acidic transactivation domain; engages the MLL and c-Myb sites of the CBP KIX domain

claims.statement: The FOXO4 transactivation domain (CR3) binds two hydrophobic pockets in the KIX domain of CBP, at the previously characterised MLL and c-Myb sites. FOXO4-CR3 shows substantially higher affinity for CBP-KIX than its homolog FOXO3a.
claims.note: Retrieved via Paperclip 2026-08-15. The KIX domain reference structure is PDB 2AGH; CBP-KIX is a globular three-helix domain with two short 3-10 helices.

claims.statement: CBP acts as a general coactivator bridging DNA-bound activators to the RNA polymerase II transcription machinery, through multiple specialised interaction domains (RID, two TAZ domains, KIX, HAT, IBiD).
claims.note: Establishes that KIX is a coactivator-bridging module mechanistically analogous to a Mediator Tail subunit, which is why this is a generalisation control.

claims.statement: Ras induces Mediator complex exchange on C/EBP-beta, reported as one of the founding demonstrations that MED23 is targeted by a transcription factor. The contact region on C/EBP-beta is not mapped.
claims.note: Mo, Kowenz-Leutz, Xu & Leutz, Mol Cell 13:241-250 (2004). PROVENANCE WARNING: this primary was NOT retrievable as full text in the Paperclip corpus. The claim rests on the citing sentence in Monte et al. 2025 (doi:10.1038/s41467-025-59014-8, ref 19). It has not been read at the source. Do not make this load-bearing until the primary is retrieved.

claims.statement: The C/EBP-beta region that contacts MED23 has never been mapped, so it is unknown whether it engages the MED23 HR2/HR3 groove used by ELK1 and ELF3.
claims.note: Absence of a mapped region in the retrieved literature. Reasoning: the ELK1 structure paper cites Mo 2004 only for the fact of Mediator exchange, never for an interface. This is the gap a peptide-tiling experiment against MED23 391-582 would close.

claims.statement: ETV1 is predicted, not observed, to present an MBM-like short linear motif to the MED23 HR2/HR3 groove, on the basis of ETS family membership plus KIT-MAPK-regulated protein stability analogous to the ELK1 mechanism.
claims.note: NO MED23 EXPERIMENT ON ETV1 EXISTS in the retrieved literature. The supporting fact — that activated KIT prolongs ETV1 protein stability while imatinib and MEK inhibition destabilize it (PMC2955195 L24) — is direct experimental evidence about ETV1 REGULATION, not about a MED23 contact, and is deliberately recorded in SOURCES.md rather than as a claim here: a regulation fact inside MediatorLink.claims would derive involvement=indirect and launder a MAPK observation into a contact. No proteome-wide MBM motif scan was executed either; the Paperclip protein VFS exposes annotation but not raw sequence. The motif scan is the first thing to run.

ELK1|MED23.sequence_note: residues 374-384 of the ELK1 transactivation domain. F378 buries deepest.
ELK1|MED23.site_note: The concave face at the HR2/HR3 interface. An eleven-residue motif in a defined groove is the tractable case - a folded-domain interface presents no comparable site.

POU2F3|POU2AF2.sequence_note: residues 188-192 in the alpha-1 helix of the POU_S domain; L235 and L237 in the alpha3-alpha4 turn add a second contact.
POU2F3|POU2AF2.site_note: A shallow, conserved groove cradling the coactivator peptide. The authors' CASTpFold pocket volume is a computation on this structure, not a measured site: ligandability here is a prediction.
